newsitem.title: CANADA: Bank Montreal CEO sees no more rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Bank Montreal CEO sees no more rate cuts.

text.p: Bank of Montreal chairman Matthew Barrett said on Wednesday that Canadian interest rates have little room to fall further after the Bank of Canada eased rates for the eight time this year earlier today.

Canada's central bank lowered its key bank rate by 25 basis points to 4.0 percent, prompting the major banks to lower their prime lending rates to 5.5 percent from 5.75 percent, their lowest level since February 1994.
"I would imagine interest rates don't have much further to go from where they are now," Barrett told reporters after giving a speech to Toronto's business community.
Barrett said he expects lower rates to spur Canada's economy, with a pick-up in Canadian gross national product in the second half of 1996 and into 1997.
"We'll see it work its way in in the last half of the year and throughout next year," Barrett said.

Canadian bank stocks rallied on the interest rate cuts. The Toronto Stock Exchange's financial services group was up 70 points in late afternoon trading. Bank of Montreal's stock gained 0.50 to 37.55 on volume of 723,000 shares.
